key_insight: 2-bit soft sensing turns marginal reads into erasures. Its real value is as the aggressive operating-point knob of the N-62 ECC-paid-capacitor family, cheapest if a logic-process periphery hosts the decoder.
killer_doubt: Signal needed scales with Q^-1(BER): raw 1e-3 vs BCH-t8's 1e-4 is 3.09 vs 3.72 sigma, only 1.2x Cs. 1 fF gives ~14 mV on 35 fF.
decisive_experiment: FPGA rig on commercial DDR5 (~$80k): sweep VARY/tRCD to emulate 1-1.5 fF margins, log 2-bit SA-timing soft data per 512 b codeword, replay through soft LDPC vs BCH t=8; synthesize the decoder in 28 nm for ns/pJ.
prior_art: Phase B N-62; in-study I-11559, I-11148, I-07888 (ADVANCE); NAND soft-sense LDPC in SSD controllers; Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010). On-die soft LDPC DRAM: none found.

key_insight: Per-bitline bonding fits: one bond anywhere along a ~20 um bitline (~0.8 um2) allows 0.5-0.8 um pitch. A logic-node periphery wafer makes ECC decoders and CCD sense nodes cheap.
killer_doubt: One periphery cannot serve all physics: charge cells sense 15-60 mV, MTJs need 10-50 uA reads, FeRAM 2-3 V plates. Sub-um hybrid bonding is fab or imec/Leti-only (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Restrict the socket to charge cells: a 180 nm programmable charge-sense periphery die, bonded to MIM 1T1C and IGZO 2T0C coupon arrays at a partner hybrid-bond line (~$600k); compare margins with monolithic test chips.
prior_art: Kioxia CBA and YMTC Xtacking (array bonded onto CMOS); Samsung/SK hynix bonded-periphery 4F2 VCT DRAM plans; CEA-Leti MAD BEOL memory platform [training knowledge].

key_insight: Voltage-coded tier selection would delete staircases and select lines. It is viable for ~4 tiers at ~0.5 V spacing; the CCD family already avoids staircases by phase-tying tiers.
killer_doubt: 32 Vt levels in ~3 V sit ~94 mV apart: 4-sigma separation needs sigma-Vt <=12 mV, under the study's 20 mV oxide drift budget. Every write rewrites the column.
decisive_experiment: 4-8 stacked IGZO TFTs on one gate with thickness-set Vt at a university fab (~$150k): per-tier Vt sigma and drift after 85 C bias stress; kill if sigma exceeds 25 mV.
prior_art: Macronix 3D vertical-gate NAND layer selection by Vt-programmed select gates (~2010) [training knowledge]; NAND wordline-stepped multi-level reads. Vt-coded 3D DRAM tiers: none found.

key_insight: Vacuum is a wear-free, trap-free barrier, and Fowler-Nordheim gives ~1e11-1e12 selectivity at V/3 for nA-class writes: a genuine transistor-free selector.
killer_doubt: A 20x20 nm island over 4 nm vacuum is ~0.9 aF: ~5 electrons at 1 V, ~90 uV on a 10 fF bitline. In-cell gain reinstates the transistor.
decisive_experiment: Do not fund standalone; fold into N-09: release 4-8 nm emitter gaps over a MOSFET floating gate (~$250k), then measure write spread, 85 C retention and emitter drift after 1e10 pulses.
prior_art: Phase B N-09 vacuum-nanogap floating node; NASA Ames nanoscale vacuum-channel transistors (Han, Meyyappan); Spindt field-emitter arrays [training knowledge].

key_insight: An indium-free ZnSnO channel is a useful resource hedge for the CCD family. Otherwise it duplicates I-00033's regenerating sense node at the top of each string.
killer_doubt: ~100 tiers at 3 gates/bit means ~300 transfers per pass: 99% charge needs CTE >=0.99997, against imec's demonstrated >98%. a-Ga2O3 mobility of <~1 cm2/Vs also slows transfers.
decisive_experiment: Add ZnSnO and a-Ga2O3 channel splits to the I-08763 planar CCD mask (~$50k extra); compare CTE versus clock and 85 C dark fill against IGZO.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD (IEDM 2024 planar; IMW 2026 vertical, via prior search logs); in-study I-10793, I-04245; Phase B N-08.

key_insight: A buried heterochannel keeps packets off interface traps. CTI is mostly modelable deferred charge, so decision feedback at the string-top sense node could relax CTE ~0.9999 toward ~0.999 (estimate).
killer_doubt: Trap kinetics, not mobility: transport over a 30 nm gate is ~15 ps at 10 cm2/Vs, yet imec shows CTE >98% at 4-6 MHz. ~120 transfers need >=0.999 each.
decisive_experiment: University-fab planar 4-phase CCDs, surface vs buried IGO/IGZO heterochannel (~$300k): CTE and deferred-charge profile vs clock 5-500 MHz at 25-125 C, replayed through a DFE corrector. Go if corrected loss <1e-3/transfer at >=100 MHz.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024; IMW 2026); LSST deferred-charge correction (Snyder 2021, via search snippet). Buried-channel or DFE-corrected oxide CCD memory: none found.

key_insight: The clearest 3D-NAND tool-reuse case: DUV only, no per-bit contact, and refresh comes free with each pass through the top amplifier.
killer_doubt: Overclaimed: a ~150 nm hole (~19,500 nm2) holding 40 packets is ~490 nm2/bit before slits, not 250. A 20 ns average needs ~3 GHz phase clocks; poly-Si traps cut CTE.
decisive_experiment: Covered by the I-08763 chip: add a poly-Si split and a 120-transfer recirculating loop to measure cumulative loss and 85 C dark fill (~$50k extra).
prior_art: Phase B N-08; imec IGZO CCD (IEDM 2024, IMW 2026); Intel 2416 and Fairchild CCD memories; in-study I-10793, I-04245.

key_insight: Circumferential magnetization round a via is closed-flux and stray-field-free; tier planes as word straps would give 100+ magnetic tiers from one hole etch.
killer_doubt: Inductive read fails: 5 nm CoFeB on a 40 nm tier links ~3e-16 Wb, ~0.1 uV for a 1 ns partial tilt. Writes need ~0.6 mA per 50 nm pillar.
decisive_experiment: Not fundable as stated. If revived, drop inductive read: test TMR/AMR readout of circumferential domains in plated NiFe/CoFeB-lined 50-100 nm vias (~$200k), measuring switching current per tier.
prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, Voyager era); in-study I-08865 (DROP, same mechanism); Phase B N-82 racetrack-in-hole; Parkin racetrack [training knowledge].

key_insight: Recomputing instead of storing is sound where near-memory compute is cheap: a PRNG seed plus a few coefficients regenerates a weight block in a few cycles.
killer_doubt: SeedLM-style seeds reach ~3-4 bits/weight, the same as deployed 4-bit formats (GPTQ, MXFP4/NVFP4): ~1-1.3x over today's baseline, not 3-8x.
decisive_experiment: Software only (~$20k GPU time): seed fitting vs GPTQ/AQLM at 2-3 bits/weight on Llama-class models, reporting perplexity and decode bytes moved.
prior_art: SeedLM (Apple, 2024 preprint) [training knowledge]; GPTQ, AWQ, AQLM; MXFP4/NVFP4 formats.

key_insight: The arithmetic holds: +1.6 eV of gap cuts intrinsic generation ~1e13x. But retention stopped being the scarce axis once oxide gain cells arrived.
killer_doubt: IGZO 2T0C is already defect- and gate-limited at <1 aA (1e3-1e4 s). a-Ga2O3 mobility ~0.1-1 cm2/Vs slows writes, and China supplies ~98% of gallium.
decisive_experiment: Only as a materials split: IGZO vs ALD a-Ga2O3 write device in one 2T0C BEOL run (~$150k); retention tails over 1e4 cells at 85-125 C and write time at 1 V.
prior_art: IGZO 2T0C gain cells (imec; Kioxia OCTRAM); in-study I-03018 Ga2O3 coaxial cell (DROP); university amorphous Ga2O3 TFT work.

key_insight: HBM4 custom base dies make memory-side gather buildable; worthwhile only for sub-32 B random words (graphs, sparse matrices).
killer_doubt: The named AI streams are already coarse: KV pages >=2 KB, embedding rows 128-512 B, MoE token blocks KBs vs 32 B sectors. Saving <~10% of HBM traffic (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Trace replay (~$30k): KV, embedding and MoE address traces through a 32 B-sector HBM model, counting PHY bytes saved versus controller-side coalescing.
prior_art: Impulse controller (Utah, 1999); GS-DRAM (MICRO 2015); RecNMP (ISCA 2020); Samsung AxDIMM; in-study I-10911 (DROP).

key_insight: A bit-plane-major layout makes precision a fetch-time knob. Its best use is MSB-plane KV scoring (I-02063) and batch-1 edge decode.
killer_doubt: Production already stores 4-bit weights, and batched decode fetches the most planes any token needs, so realistic savings are ~1.1-1.3x of decode traffic (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Software emulation (~$30k): a plane-fetch policy on Llama-class decode at batch 1/32/128 versus static 4-bit, measuring bytes moved and accuracy.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024); Matryoshka Quantization (ICML 2025); Stripes bit-serial accelerator; in-study I-02063 (HOLD), I-05653 and I-09970 (DROP).
